messages:
Ana (PM): Quick huddle — runtime perf OKR planning for next quarter. Need to pick 1 customer-facing win + 1 infra win. Rough targets? :wave:
Mike (eng-runtime): My vote: KV prefix caching first for hosted chat. Big wins for p95 and cost on repeated prompts. Target: 25% p95 latency reduction on chat 90/180 seqs, 30% token cost drop for common prompts.
Sasha (ML): Agree KV is high ROI. Also pushing quantization/8-bit kernel project — much bigger cost savings long-term but QA risk.
Jordan (Infra): Resource note: week-of rollout for KV needs a dedicated staging pool; we only have 2 extra nodes in eu-west. Might need to phase region-by-region.
Alice (ProdOps): Launch criteria we should set now: canary shows <2% quality regression on eval set, <5% error increase, and automatic fallback to FP16 variant. Also need runbook for incidents.
Mike (eng-runtime): For kernels: if we prioritize fused attention kernels (CUDA+XLA paths) we can get 10-15% throughput improvement for long seqs. That is faster to prototype than full quantized runtime. Suggest split roadmap: Q1 sprint -> kernels + KV, Q2 -> quant/8-bit rollout with eval harness.
Sasha (ML): For quant rollout we need strict eval gating. Proposed metric: perplexity delta <= 0.8% on our regression suite and average human rating delta <= 0.5 points on targeted prompts. If fail, auto-block.
Ana (PM): OKR draft ideas: 1) Reduce hosted-chat p95 by 25% (baseline: 320ms) 2) Reduce per-token hosted cost for top-10 customers by 30% 3) Ship canary for fused kernels with 99.9% availability during test window. Thoughts?
Jordan (Infra): Also add an infra-level OKR: "Deploy KV caching to Dedicated pools with canary routing in 3 regions" — that'll exercise our routing/fallback logic.
Alice (ProdOps): Need observable milestones: data retention for KV metrics, dashboards for cache hit rates, token-cost per request breakdown. Ops will own alert thresholds.
Mike (eng-runtime): Tradeoffs: If we push kernels first, we can show quick wins and reduce pressure on infra. If we go quant-first, we risk more rollbacks but higher long-term savings. Recommend kernels+KV first as Ana suggested.
Sasha (ML): Agree. We'll start eval harness work in parallel so that quant rollout is ready by Q2 if kernels+KV go smoothly.
Ana (PM): Action items: @Mike add proposal + rough ETA for KV canary (due Fri). @Sasha draft eval gating thresholds and automated tests (due Mon). @Jordan map staging capacity and region rollout plan (due Tue). @Alice create dashboards and runbook template (due Wed).
perf-bot: Summary saved to /docs/rt-perf/quarterly-planning/1765504321-summary.md :white_check_mark:
Mike (eng-runtime): I'll post the KV canary design in #eng-runtime-design once I have ETA.
Sasha (ML): I'll attach small sample eval results when ready.
Ana (PM): Great — next sync same time next week to confirm priorities. :calendar:
